result.title: Agnostic Learning by Imitating
result.summary: Given a class of machine learning models and sample access to a data distribution with binary labels, which computational task is harder: training a discriminative model that distinguishes positive and negative labels as well as the best member of the class, or training a generative model whose outputs are indistinguishable from real data by all members of the class? We prove that these two fundamental tasks in computational learning theory are not just closely related, but actually equivalent to each other in complexity. One direction of this equivalence was previously known. Indeed, the powerful regularity lemma in complexity theory gives an efficient oracle reduction from the indistinguishability task (a.k.a. multiaccuracy) to the distinguishing task (a.k.a. agnostic learning) in the style of boosting algorithms. Our main contribution is an efficient oracle reduction in the other direction. Taking this idea further, we show that a multiaccuracy oracle is a remarkably powerful primitive, achieving not just agnostic learning but also a wide range of seemingly more demanding learning objectives via similarly efficient and direct constructions. Our results crucially use the power of making adaptive queries to the oracle, and stand in stark contrast to prior work, which showed that post-processing a single multiaccurate predictor is insufficient for even weak forms of learning. On a technical level, we draw a connection between our (offline) problem and a version of no-regret learning in the online setting, which allows us to use follow-the-leader type algorithms to modify the label distribution and aggregate the predictions of the multiaccuracy oracle.

AI.brief_summary: 该文证明 agnostic learning 与 multiaccuracy（输出对类内所有判别器都不可区分）在 oracle 归约下复杂度等价，主要给出从 agnostic 学习预言机到 multiaccuracy 的高效归约，并借自适应查询把该原语推广到更多学习目标。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「不可区分 vs 可区分」的等价视角与自适应查询归约，可能为设计检验 latent 是否保留视觉证据、以及贡献分配的评价判据提供概念借鉴，具体可用性需核查。
